transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because for the last year or so, I just... I can't seem to sit down. I'm always puttering around, fixing things, arranging... or volunteering for one more thing. Even at 87, I just have a hard time being still. That's really it.
Are you currently taking any antipsychotic medications, or have you started any new medications in the past year or so?
No... no, I don't take anything like that. And I haven't started anything new, either. Just... just the same things I've been taking for a while.
Have you noticed any unexplained weight loss, feeling unusually warm or sweaty, or a racing heartbeat along with this restlessness?
No... I haven't noticed anything like that. My weight is fine, and... no racing heart or anything. Just what I mentioned before.
Over this past year, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually low or sad, or on the other hand, unusually elevated, cheerful, or irritable?
No, not really. My mood has been... fine, I suppose. Just normal.

When you feel this need to keep moving or stay busy, do you also notice worried or anxious thoughts running through your mind, or is it more just a physical urge to move without any accompanying worry?
No... I don't think so. I'm not really worried about anything. It's just... a feeling that I need to be doing something. Just physical, I suppose.
Have you ever, at any point in your life, taken an antipsychotic medication or a strong anti-nausea drug like metoclopramide or prochlorperazine, even if it was many years ago?
No... I don't believe so. Not that I can recall, anyway. I haven't taken anything like that.
Do you notice that this urge to move gets worse when you're sitting or lying still, and feels better once you start moving around?
I... I don't really know. I haven't noticed it working quite like that. I just... I just like to be doing things, I suppose.
Do you notice this urge to move is mainly in your legs, especially in the evening or at night when you're trying to rest, along with an uncomfortable or tingling sensation in them?
No... I haven't noticed any tingling. And it's not really just in my legs. I just... well, I don't have anything like that at night.
Have you or your family noticed any recent changes in your memory, thinking, or ability to keep track of things over this past year?
No... I don't think so. My memory is fine. My family hasn't... well, they haven't said anything to me about it. I keep track of things well enough.
When you feel this urge to stay busy, does it bother or distress you, or does it just feel like a normal part of who you are?
No... it doesn't bother me. I suppose it's just normal for me. I don't really think about it much... it's just how I am, really.
